result.name: Warehouse.Activity.Get
result.description: Reads open warehouse activities with optional header, document and line filters.
result.selectionDescription: Read-only. Reads open warehouse picks and put-aways; use Warehouse.BinContent.Get for bin stock.

subject.description: Optional Warehouse Activity Header SystemId or activity number; omit it to read a collection.

target.description: The SystemId of the Warehouse Activity Header.
The number of the Warehouse Activity.
The SystemId of the Warehouse Activity Header.
The number of the Warehouse Activity.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of matching records to skip. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to the platform page size.

parameters.name: activityType
parameters.description: Warehouse activity type, for example Pick or Put-away.

parameters.name: systemId
parameters.description: Warehouse Activity Header SystemId. recordSystemId and id are accepted too.

parameters.name: whseDocumentNo
parameters.description: Filter activities by source warehouse document number.

parameters.name: includeLines
parameters.description: Include the activity lines in each result.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Success on a successful call; Error responses use the standard error envelope.

fields.name: noOfRecords
fields.description: Total matching open activities before paging.

fields.name: result
fields.description: The paged open Warehouse Activity Header rows.

errors.when: No Warehouse Activity Header identifier was supplied.
errors.fix: Send subject or an identifier under data.

errors.when: The supplied identifier does not match a Warehouse Activity Header.
errors.fix: Check the value or look the record up first.

errors.when: Two supplied identifiers point to different warehouse activities.
errors.fix: Send one identifier or identifiers for the same warehouse activity.
errors.nextStep: Send one identifier or identifiers for the same warehouse activity.

errors.when: An identifier cannot be read in the expected format.
errors.fix: Send a GUID for SystemId keys and a document number for No. keys.

errors.when: activityType is not a valid warehouse activity type.
errors.fix: Use a value from the Warehouse Activity Type enum.

effect.changes: Reads open Warehouse Activity Header and Line records and changes nothing.

related.name: Warehouse.BinContent.Get
related.useInsteadWhen: Use it to read bin stock rather than open warehouse activities.

result.overview: Read-only access to open Warehouse Activity Header records, optionally including their lines and source-document filter.

conventions.errorsAndWarnings:
## Errors and warnings
An error response has `status` = `Error`, a stable `code`, the `error` text and, when they apply, `parameter` (the request parameter concerned, e.g. `lines[2].no`), `received` (the value received), `expected` (what was expected) and `nextStep` (what to do now). `hint` says where to read more.
When a request has several problems, all of them are listed in `errors[]` - each with the same fields - under a top-level `code` (`MultipleErrors`, or a shared code such as `InvalidLine` for the `lines` of a Create type) and a summary `error`. Fix them all before calling again. One problem is reported at the top level, with no `errors[]`.
Request values are checked first and every problem found is reported together. A Business Central validation error raised afterwards, while a record is being written, stops the call and is reported on its own: `code` = `BusinessCentralError`, Business Central's own `error` text, and `parameter` naming the request parameter being applied, e.g. `lines[1].accountNo`. Nothing is written.
Request values are read in one format, whatever the language: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; date-times ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset; amounts as JSON numbers (or a string such as `"1234.56"`, no thousands separator); integers as JSON integers; booleans `true` or `false`. Any other value is `InvalidParameterFormat` with `received` and `expected`; for an unambiguous local form such as `26.09.2026`, `nextStep` gives the value to resend. Every bad value of a request is reported together.
Answers are written in one format as well, whatever the language of the call: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times ISO 8601, numbers with a dot and no thousands separator, and the option and enum values of every answer except `Data.Records.Get` and `Data.Records.Set` as their English names, so a value read from an answer can be sent back. Those two answer the caption of the language of the call, for a person to read. The language of the call (`lcid`) changes captions and message texts, not these forms. Two things are outside Bifrost's control: Business Central writes its own texts (a ledger entry description such as `Direct Cost V00010 on 10/02/26`, the text of a `BusinessCentralError`) with the regional settings of the server session, which `lcid` does not change, so a date in such a text can be in month-day order; and a table view is read with those settings too, so write dates in a view as `YYYY-MM-DD` and decimals with a dot.
Both success and error responses can carry `warnings[]`, each with `code`, `message` and, when they apply, `parameter` and `nextStep`.
`UnknownParameter` normally warns about undeclared data keys without changing status, validationResult or domain warningCount. Set the root envelope option `strict:true` (next to type and subject, never inside data) to refuse every unknown key before execution. Strict refusals list the keys and localized nextStep corrections; no business changes or successful execution charges occur. With strict omitted or false, warnings join success and error responses as before. Example: {"type":"Memory.User.Set","strict":true,"data":{"memory":"test","memry":"typo"}} is refused.
`FieldChangedByBC` is a warning from Data.Records.Set: another field validation or the write changed a sent field after its own validation. `parameter` names data[n].fields.{jsonName}, counting from 0. Status stays Success. Compare the returned values with what you sent; follow `nextStep` to use validation order or send the field again in a separate call. Normalisation of the field itself, LCY, Dimension Set ID, BLOB, Media, MediaSet and skipped fields are excluded.
`Retryable` means a transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. `error` keeps Business Central's original text. `expected` is "no concurrent lock on the same records"; `nextStep` is "Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed." Bifrost does not retry automatically. Other platform errors, including uncaught queue-path errors, remain `BusinessCentralError`.
Codes: `MissingParameter`, `InvalidParameterFormat`, `InvalidParameter`, `RecordNotFound`, `AmbiguousRecord`, `ConflictingIdentifiers`, `InvalidFilterField`, `InvalidLine`, `NothingToPreview`, `LinesSkipped`, `BlockedByWriteGuard`, `PreconditionFailed`, `PermissionDenied`, `LimitExceeded`, `BusinessCentralError`, `MultipleErrors`, `DeprecatedParameter`, `UnknownParameter`, `FieldChangedByBC`, `Retryable`. The `error` text may be translated; the code never is.
